brief.headline: Seventh night of port strikes; Graham sanctions bill gains momentum
brief.lead: Channels celebrated a sustained Russian air campaign against Ukraine's Black Sea ports as the day's dominant story, while sounding alarm over a US Senate sanctions bill crossing its sponsorship threshold. Overall tone was mixed—triumphant on strikes and the front, defensive on Western pressure.

developments.title: Seventh consecutive night of strikes on Odesa-region ports
developments.body: Multiple channels claimed Russian strikes on Odesa, Chornomorsk, Mykolaiv and Pivdennyi ports, hitting drone assembly facilities, fuel reserves and cargo ships; Two Majors claimed a Mykolaiv strike damaged three foreign vessels and killed two Ukrainians, while Poddubny claimed 24 vessels sunk. All figures are channel/MoD-adjacent claims, unconfirmed.

developments.title: Claimed advances near Chasiv Yar, Kupyansk, Sumy and Zaporizhzhia
developments.body: Channels reported Russian gains around Konstantinovka and Chasiv Yar, aviation destroying Ukrainian reserves near Chorne (Kupyansk), and the Sever grouping claiming 50 settlements captured in 2026 reaching Bachevsk. WarGonzo also cited advances near Hulyaipole and Red Lyman. All unconfirmed operational claims.

developments.title: Graham sanctions bill crosses 61-sponsor threshold, alarming Rybar
developments.body: Rybar flagged that the US Senate's Graham 'Sanctioning Russia Act' attracted 61 bipartisan sponsors, surpassing the passage threshold. Framed alongside EU's first sanctions citing strikes on Kyiv (targeting ABS Electro drone-component makers).

developments.title: Zelensky's dismissal of defense minister framed as Western-noted misstep
developments.body: Rybar and Two Majors highlighted Western media criticism of Zelensky for dismissing 'reform-minded' defense minister Fedorov, with Two Majors describing Ukrainian youth protests demanding more aggressive action. Part of a coordinated 'Kyiv in disarray' narrative.

developments.title: Russian blogger arrested for 'fake news' about army
developments.body: WarGonzo reported blogger Ilya Remeslo arrested in St. Petersburg for allegedly spreading fake news about the army—a notable internal-security signal amid channels' usual pro-military tone.

developments.title: Grain export data undercuts strike-damage claims
developments.body: Rybar acknowledged Ukrainian port traffic rose to 42.4M tons and grain exports grew despite 23 Russian strikes hitting 1,002 infrastructure targets—an unusually candid admission that the port campaign hasn't halted throughput.

narrative_watch.title: 'Kyiv embraces Nazi ideals' framing
narrative_watch.body: Kotsnews amplified plans to rebury UPA nationalist leader Konovalets as proof of Zelensky's alleged Nazi sympathies, part of a recurring delegitimization line targeting Ukrainian leadership.

narrative_watch.title: West as encircling aggressor
narrative_watch.body: Rybar strung together US drone surveillance around China/NK, NATO reconnaissance over Crimea, Poland/ESA Warsaw security center, and the Zangezur corridor to portray a globally encircling West.

narrative_watch.title: Caution against drone-only triumphalism
narrative_watch.body: NgP raZVedka warned Russia against illusions that drones alone can defeat Western weapons and tactics—a rare self-critical note against prevailing tech-optimism.

mood_lines.text: Triumphant over seventh straight night of port strikes, though Rybar quietly concedes grain and cargo throughput keeps rising.
Upbeat on claimed advances across Kupyansk, Sumy, Chasiv Yar and Zaporizhzhia; consistently positive tone, all figures unconfirmed.
Most negative topic; alarm over Graham sanctions bill, EU measures and NATO encirclement across multiple theaters.
Mixed: naval aviation anniversary pride offset by blogger arrest, rising gas prices and drone-doctrine caution.
Uniformly negative, focused on Zelensky's minister purge, alleged Nazi glorification and Ukrainian command dysfunction.
Single post reframed a Ukrainian Geran drone hit on a cargo ship as intercepting Western military supplies.

flag_texts.title: Russia internal sentiment swings to neutral
flag_texts.body: Net sentiment moved +38 to zero as celebratory naval-aviation content was balanced by negative items: blogger Remeslo's arrest, rising gas prices, and warnings against drone-only overconfidence.

flag_texts.title: Criticism turns uniformly negative
flag_texts.body: Net dropped 29 points to -100 as all six posts hammered Ukraine—Zelensky's Fedorov dismissal, the Konovalets reburial, and command inefficiency—with no offsetting content.

flag_texts.title: Mobilisation and Putin-criticism watchlists quiet
flag_texts.body: No mobilisation-rumour or Putin-criticism posts surfaced today; the sole mobilisation-tagged item was a positive note on the SVOD digital battlefield system, not manpower concerns.
